Nov 20, 2026

Agents SDK now supports Pi 1.6 with tools that wait without keeping your agent awake

Agents

Agents SDK v0.34.0 upgrades PiHarness to Pi 1.6 ↗︎. A Pi tool can now wait for a person, a deadline, or another session without keeping the Durable Object awake, and a session can start from a history that your application already has.

Tools that wait

  • Park until a signal or a deadline. A tool can return a park instead of a result, and Pi runs it again when a signal arrives or the deadline passes. While it waits, the call holds no invocation, so the Durable Object can hibernate. Deliver signals with the new harness.signal(). Refer to Tools that wait.
  • Wait for a subagent. submit() and continue() take notify, so a parked tool wakes when another session's input settles. Refer to Wait for a subagent.
  • Approval gates. A beforeTool hook can park a tool call before it runs, for example until a person approves it.

Session updates

  • Start a session from an existing history. harness.root(), sessions.create(), and sessions.fork() take Pi's init, which writes messages into the transcript in the commit that creates the session. The root session is now created on its first use, so harness.root() can seed it. Refer to Seed a session with an existing history.
  • Keep queued input across an abort. With submit(input, { onAbort: "keep" }), stopping an answer does not drop the message that the user or another agent sent next.
  • Steadier runs. Pi retries more dropped provider connections. When Anthropic can no longer continue a message thread, agents/models/pi-ai sends the whole conversation again instead of failing the turn. PiHarness.dispose() frees Pi AI's per-session state.

Wait for a person's answer

This tool asks the user a question, then parks until your agent delivers the answer:

While the question is open, the session's run is still going, and the object can hibernate or be evicted. harness.signal() wakes the object, and Pi runs the tool again with the answer.

Other changes

  • MCP re-authorization. A request that needs the user to sign in again throws MCPAuthorizationRequiredError with a link. A failed server stays failed until you call the new reconnectMcpServer(id). Refer to Failures and reconnecting.
  • Failed requests no longer send error details. A failed request gets a generic 500 response, and a failed WebSocket upgrade closes with code 1011. Use onFetchError() to choose the response. Refer to Failed requests.
  • Chat fixes. Stop, clear, regenerate, and resume now work across tabs and during recovery.
  • Scheduling fixes. A schedule, queue item, or Task run that is cancelled or replaced no longer runs again.
  • Models. ai.image() and Pi AI's ai.images() run the FLUX.2 image models. claudeCode() defaults to claude-sonnet-5-5. Examples move off the Workers AI models retired on November 20, 2026.

Upgrade

Once a conversation runs on Pi 1.6, Pi 1.5 cannot run its tool calls or model requests. After upgrading, roll forward to fix deployment issues rather than rolling back to Pi 1.5.

Deliver signals with harness.signal() instead of (await harness.pi()).signal(), and call harness.root() before you reach the root session through harness.pi(). If you use Pi Durable directly, RunEndTask is now HookTask, and code mode namespaces come from Extension.namespace. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.6.0 changelog ↗︎ for the full list of breaking changes.

If you use the MCP client, catch MCPAuthorizationRequiredError and send the user to error.authUrl, and give users a way to call reconnectMcpServer(id) for a failed server. If you relied on error details in failed responses, implement onFetchError().

The Agents SDK v0.34.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Nov 3, 2026

Agents SDK now supports Pi 1.5 with fewer storage writes and lower memory use

Agents

Agents SDK v0.33.0 upgrades PiHarness to Pi 1.5 ↗︎. The release reduces storage transactions while streaming, improves throughput across many sessions, and reduces memory use when streaming large tool calls.

Performance improvements

  • Far fewer storage writes while streaming. Pi stores streamed answers and tool output in batches, within a second of each update, instead of on every update. Over SQLite, this cuts storage transactions by about 27x for long answers and 5.7x for turns with parallel tools, and CPU by about a quarter.
  • Higher throughput across many sessions. Pi's scheduler no longer rechecks every conversation on each commit. In a SQLite benchmark with 2,048 sessions, one Pi harness went from 88 to 459 agent runs per second.
  • Less memory on large answers. Streaming a 500 KB tool call used to take about 20 seconds of CPU and a 100 MB heap. Pi now appends new text instead of copying it on every update.

Streaming updates remain visible immediately, but are persisted in batches. With the default settings, a crash can lose up to about one second of streamed progress. Refer to Recovery to configure this interval.

Session and tool updates

  • A view of each session. session.watch() replaces session.events(). It returns the newest transcript entries and the session's live state, such as the answer being streamed, running tools, and why the last run ended without an answer.
  • Continue without adding a message. The new session.continue() API starts a new run using the existing transcript, for example after a model error or when a run reaches its turn limit.
  • Turn limit. defaults.maxTurns caps the tool rounds a run can take in new sessions.
  • Tasks that keep crashing end. Pi now ends a task cut off by its restart limit instead of parking it. retry() and the parked status are removed.
  • Browser in Pi's code mode. Scripts in Pi's code mode can call browserTool and pass its screenshots to image(). browserTool also stops when the harness aborts its call.

Continue an unanswered conversation

For an existing session and submission operationId, check the result before offering a continuation. For example, after resolving a model error:

This starts a new run without appending a user message. The session must be idle. If the transcript already ends in an answer, the operation returns unanswered with reason nothing_to_answer. Refer to Work with sessions.

Upgrade

Once a conversation runs on Pi 1.5, Pi 1.4 cannot read it. After upgrading, roll forward to fix deployment issues rather than rolling back to Pi 1.4.

Update callers of session.events() to use session.watch(), and remove uses of retry() and the parked status. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.5.0 changelog ↗︎ for the full list of breaking changes.

The Agents SDK v0.33.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Oct 29, 2026

Agents SDK: Agent Skills are files in your agent's Workspace

Agents

Agent Skills in the Cloudflare Agents SDK are now files. Write a folder with a SKILL.md into your agent's Computer ↗︎ Workspace, under /workspace/.agents/skills/, and the agent can use it on its next turn. You do not need a build step or a deploy, and the agent can write its own skills.

This release includes:

  • Three sources. Load skills from a Computer Workspace, an R2 bucket, or code. Think lists every source again before each turn.
  • The open format. Every SKILL.md is checked against the Agent Skills specification ↗︎. As the specification's guide for agents recommends, a skill that breaks a rule still loads, with a logged warning. Use parseSkill() to check a skill before you write it.
  • Scripts in the Workspace. Skill scripts are Workspace files, and the model runs them with the Workspace exec tool. Refer to Execution.
  • Skill tools for any harness. Use the same activate_skill and read_skill_resource tools in Think, Pi Durable, or the AI SDK. Refer to Skills tools.
  • Warm prompt caches. When a skill changes mid-conversation, Think sends the new catalog as a reminder instead of rebuilding the cached system prompt. An overridden getSystemPrompt() now stays at the top of the system prompt, above context blocks.

This is a breaking change for code that uses agents/skills directly. The agents:skills Vite import, agents/skills/compile, SkillRegistry, and Think's skillWorkspace are removed, and runner() moved to agents/skills/runner. Install Agents SDK v0.32.0 ↗︎ and Think v0.23.0 ↗︎ or later. Refer to the computer-skills ↗︎ and r2-skills ↗︎ examples.

Oct 28, 2026

Agents SDK: Preview dev servers in the browser without public URLs

AgentsBrowser Run

Agents that build websites need to check their work in a real browser. Internal hostnames let your agent's browser preview a dev server running in a container without exposing that server to the public Internet.

With internal hostnames, the persistent browser in the Cloudflare Agents SDK can open sites that only your agent serves. Give the browser hostnames such as preview.internal, and its requests to them go to your agent instead of the Internet. The model can check a dev server in its sandbox, a folder in its workspace, or another Worker in the same browser it uses for the web, and nothing is exposed publicly.

Each internal host has a fetch function that runs in your Durable Object, so it can use the object's bindings and state. A host can also send its requests straight to another Worker through a service binding. Add a target schema to a host, and the model chooses what it serves, such as which port or which folder.

Internal hostnames are a capability of the browser, independent of your agent harness. Use the built-in adapters for Pi Durable, AI SDK, and TanStack AI, or connect another harness by implementing a tool with browser.session(). No prebuilt adapter is required.

This example adds a private dev-server preview to a Pi Durable agent. Start with that guide's packages, bindings, and request handler, and install Agents SDK v0.31.0 ↗︎ or later. The example has three parts:

  • Browser configuration: internalHosts defines how the browser reaches the dev server.
  • Durable Object wiring: Lifecycle and fetchInternalHost() connect the browser to your application.
  • Harness integration: browserTool from agents/browser/pi registers the tool with Pi.

To use another harness, keep the browser configuration. Choose a browser-tool adapter if one is available, or implement a tool using browser.session().

browserTool tells the model about each host, including the schema of its target. Because preview.internal has a target schema, the model can choose which port it serves. To check its dev server, the model calls browser.assignHost() with a target that matches the schema, such as { port: 5173 }, and opens the URL it gets back:

The target is checked against the schema and stored, so it lasts across turns, browser restarts, and redeploys. Each request to http://preview.internal/ then calls the host's fetch function with { port: 5173 }.

This release also simplifies browserTool. It runs the model's code in its own Dynamic Worker and no longer needs a CodemodeRuntime export. Refer to the v0.31.0 upgrade notes ↗︎ if you already use browserTool.

For the complete example, limits, and security guidance, refer to Internal hostnames.

Oct 26, 2026

Cloudflare Computer now helps agents recover from interruptions and wait for approval

AgentsWorkers

@cloudflare/computer ↗︎ gives your agent a workspace to run code in. From v0.7.0, that code can resume after a deploy or crash, and pause on an external action, for example to approve a tool call.

Resume interrupted runs

Set onInterrupt: "replay" on WorkerJavaScriptBackend, or on a single run.

When recovery is triggered, the JavaScript runs again from the beginning, reusing recorded results for completed calls without printing previously recorded output again. If a call's result was not recorded before the interruption, recovery may repeat the call — even if its action already succeeded. For retry handling, including unsafeToRepeat() for operations that cannot safely repeat, refer to Calls that must not run twice.

Recovery starts on the next call to workspace.runtime. To recover without waiting for traffic, call workspace.runtime.recover() from a Durable Object alarm.

Wait for approvals

Expose your application functions through custom modules. A function can call ctx.interrupt() to pause the run until your application supplies an approval decision.

Require approval before posting a comment

For example, to provide a GitHub module that allows an agent to post a comment on an issue with approval, an implementation of postComment could look like this:

Call it from agent code

When the agent's code calls postComment(), the run pauses at ctx.interrupt() until your app responds. The agent's code calls it like any other function:

Respond to the approval request

The time spent waiting does not count toward its timeout. The wait also survives deploys. Fetch the pending calls with workspace.runtime.pending() and resolve them with respond():

The run continues once all pending calls are resolved.

For setup, current limitations, and how replay works, refer to Resume runs after a restart.

Cloudflare MCP servers no longer serve /sse

Agents

Cloudflare's product-specific MCP servers now serve only /mcp. A request to /sse returns 410 Gone with the server's /mcp URL, which most MCP clients show in their connection error.

Oct 22, 2026

Agents SDK now supports the latest Pi 1.4 release

Agents

Agents SDK v0.30.0 runs PiHarness on Pi 1.4 ↗︎, and makes it recover more reliably from evictions, crashes, and storage errors.

  • Hibernation while Pi's tasks sleep. PiHarness passes Pi's new onWake callback to your harness factory. While a task sleeps, such as during a model retry backoff, the Durable Object can hibernate until the task is due instead of staying in memory.
  • Parked tasks. Pi 1.4 parks a task that keeps crashing the object instead of restarting it forever. Parked operations show as parked in pending(), and session.retry() runs them again.
  • Recovery from storage errors. PiHarness reopens Pi after a storage error instead of failing every call until the object restarts. Its wake-up job retries failed steps with a backoff instead of being dropped.
  • Retried model streams. agents/models/pi-ai reports a cut-off or idle model stream as a transient error, so Pi retries the turn instead of failing it.

Upgrade

The Agents SDK v0.30.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Pi 1.4 migrates the session storage in the object's SQLite database to a schema that Pi 1.3 cannot open, so a deployment cannot roll back past this upgrade. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.4.0 changelog ↗︎ for Pi's own breaking changes.

Oct 21, 2026

createAI replaces workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider

AgentsWorkers AIAI Gateway

The Agents SDK has a new createAI function for the AI SDK and Pi AI. It unifies what workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider did: Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes, and vendor models, through the AI binding or an account id and API token.

workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider are now feature frozen and marked as deprecated. Please migrate at your convenience.

With createAI you get:

  • Every model by id. Workers AI @cf/ ids, any model in the AI Gateway catalog, and dynamic routes as dynamic/<route>.
  • Vendor model objects. Pass a model from the vendor's own package, such as ai(anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")). It goes unchanged to AI Gateway's provider-native endpoint.
  • The binding, or an account id and API token. Use a gateway in another account, or call from outside a Worker.
  • Gateway options, fallback, and BYOK. Caching, logging, metadata, retries, byokAlias, zdr, and vendorKey.
  • Stream resume. Through the binding, a catalog or dynamic route stream that drops mid-answer resumes.
  • Other model types. Embeddings, images, speech, transcription, and reranking in the AI SDK provider, and images in Pi AI.
Before After
createWorkersAI({ binding }) createAI({ binding })
createWorkersAI({ accountId, apiKey }) createAI({ accountId, apiToken })
createAiGateway(...) createAI(...), with fallback for a list of models
createAISearch from workers-ai-provider createAISearchNamespace from ai-search-provider

For AI Search, use ai-search-provider. For more information, refer to Models.

Think agents now use a @cloudflare/computer workspace

AgentsWorkers

Think and Agent Skills now use the workspace from @cloudflare/computer ↗︎ as well as the filesystem tools. A JavaScript execution environment can be configured by adding the WorkerJavaScriptBackend.

@cloudflare/shell is deprecated, and so is Think's createExecuteTool. These will no longer be developed nor supported from today onwards.

Oct 19, 2026

Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization

Agents

The Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization ↗︎.

Grant only the required scopes when you connect, then authorize more on demand as your agent performs a task. When a tool call needs a scope you have not granted, the server returns an insufficient_scope challenge ↗︎ naming it, and your MCP client asks you to approve it. Scopes you already granted are kept.

To start with the least access, choose Minimal on the consent page when you connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Refer to authorization in MCP.

Available now in all MCP clients that support step-up authorization.

Oct 13, 2026

Cloudflare API MCP server sends Workers Issues as MCP Events

AgentsWorkers

Workers Issues provides built-in error monitoring for Cloudflare Workers. It detects production failures and groups related failures into issues without an SDK or application wrapper.

The Cloudflare API MCP server now sends these issues as MCP Events ↗︎, the first event it exposes. MCP clients discover cloudflare.alert.workers_observability_real_time_issue with events/list and subscribe with events/subscribe, scoped to an account or a single Worker. When Issues detects a new or recurring issue, the server posts a signed event to the client's webhook, so an agent can start investigating without polling.

To use it, enable Issues on your Worker and connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp with the Notifications Write and Workers Observability Write permissions to a client that supports MCP Events webhooks.

New persistent browser tool in the Agents SDK, with tabs and logins that last between turns

Agents

The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a browserTool that gives your agent a Browser Run browser it can return to on later turns. Your agent can open a website, inspect a page, and come back to it with its tabs, cookies, and login session intact while the browser session remains alive.

When you give browserTool to your agent, the model writes code that drives the browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Screenshots return as images that an image-capable model can inspect and your UI can display.

To use browserTool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.28.0 ↗︎ or greater installed. Create a Browser, register it with your object's Lifecycle, and add the tool to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

Each Pi conversation gets its own active tab by default. Cookies and logins remain shared within the browser.

The browser stays alive between turns, including when the Durable Object hibernates. Its default idle timeout is 10 minutes. If the session expires or crashes, the tool creates a fresh browser and reports restarted: true. The old tabs and login state are gone.

You can also use the persistent browser with the AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters, or connect another harness through the public Browser and CDP APIs.

Refer to persistent browser tools for the complete Pi Durable example, required bindings, and behavior when a tool call is interrupted.

Oct 12, 2026

New web_fetch tool in the Agents SDK for reading webpages and documents, with automatic markdown conversion

Agents

The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a web_fetch tool that reads webpages, PDFs, and supported Office documents, using Workers AI Markdown Conversion to turn them into text the model can read. The tool requests Markdown directly from sites that support Markdown for Agents and formats JSON for the model.

When you give the web_fetch tool to your agent, the model provides a URL and receives back the page content, along with the final URL, HTTP status, and content type. Long pages come back in smaller sections, with an offset the model can use to continue reading. You control which hosts the agent can fetch, response size, timeouts, and redirects.

When you also provide the web_search tool to your agent, the model is told to use web_fetch to read the pages that web_search returns.

To use the web_fetch tool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.28.0 ↗︎ or greater installed, and add it to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

The web_fetch tool works with any harness. The SDK includes AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters. If you use a different harness, or need to fetch a page without calling a model, use fetchWeb(), windowWebFetchPage(), and renderWebFetchPage() from agents/webfetch. Direct fetching does not require a Durable Object or browser.

For setup, examples, and request controls, refer to Web fetch.

Oct 2, 2026

Run the Pi Durable harness on Cloudflare with the Agents SDK

AgentsWorkers

The Agents SDK now provides first-class support for building agents using the Pi harness. You can build long-running agents using the combination of Pi 1.0 ↗︎, Pi Durable ↗︎, and the new PiHarness class that the Cloudflare Agents SDK provides, ensuring your agent's work is durably persisted, even if interrupted mid-turn.

Built with Earendil ↗︎, this integration is our first step toward first-class support for third-party agent harnesses on Cloudflare.

Beta

PiHarness is in beta. Pi Durable ↗︎ is a new, experimental package, and the PiHarness API will likely change as Pi Durable matures.

PiHarness is a new "Lifecycle capability" provided by the Cloudflare Agents SDK. Pi Durable provides the agent harness and the Lifecycle is responsible for keeping the agent running in the Durable Object. The Lifecycle is a core concept in the Agents SDK ensuring that long-running work can run in a Durable Object, surviving restarts, crashes, and network issues. We will share more on Lifecycle capabilities in the near future.

Install

npm i agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
yarn add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
pnpm add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
bun add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai

Both Pi packages are optional peer dependencies of agents, so you only install them if you use the harness.

Use it in an Agent

Creating a Pi agent requires configuring the Pi Harness with a model, skills, and tools, then registering the PiHarness with the Agent class.

The agents/models/pi-ai entry point supports AI Gateway and Workers AI models, so you can get started with Cloudflare models right away or use your existing Pi AI provider.

Add tools with extensions

Both tools and system prompt sections are provided to the Pi Harness via extensions.

For more information on creating and configuring extensions, refer to Extensions.

Oct 1, 2026

The best way to do MCP auth just got better: Workers OAuth Provider goes v1, with a new split API and full support for MCP 2026-07-28

AgentsWorkers

@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider ↗︎ is now v1, with a new split API. One Worker acts as the authorization server: it signs users in and issues tokens. Your MCP server acts as the resource server, and can run in another Worker. It validates each token with the authorization server over a Service Binding, without crossing the public Internet.

  • It supports the MCP 2026-07-28 authorization specification ↗︎, including Client ID Metadata Documents ↗︎ and issuer identification ↗︎. It still works with older clients, including those using Dynamic Client Registration ↗︎.
  • insufficientScope() gives you step-up authorization ↗︎ in one line.
  • The authorization server and the resource server can run in different Workers ↗︎ with different WAF and rate limiting rules.
  • One authorization server can issue tokens for many MCP servers ↗︎.
  • A migration skill ↗︎ ships in the npm package so a coding agent can perform the upgrade.

The split API

In the example, env.AUTH_SERVER.validateToken is that Service Binding call. The calendar Worker needs no KV namespace of its own.

OAuthResourceServer publishes the RFC 9728 ↗︎ protected resource metadata that MCP clients use to find your authorization server. It answers requests without a token with a 401 challenge that points to that metadata. It also rejects tokens issued for any other resource.

You can still use OAuthProvider as both the authorization server and the MCP server. For most 0.x deployments, the only required change is to add resourceMetadata: { resource }.

Other updates and helpers

  • Consent page ↗︎ and upstream sign-in ↗︎ helpers implement the MCP confused deputy protections.
  • Sliding refresh token expiry ↗︎ with refreshTokenIdleTTL.
  • Resumable KV cleanup ↗︎ with purgeExpiredData().
  • An internal reason ↗︎ on every error passed to onError.

Upgrade with the migration skill

npm i @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
yarn add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
pnpm add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
bun add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest

Point your coding agent at node_modules/@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/skills/migrate-to-1.x/SKILL.md, or follow the migration guide ↗︎.

For both Workers in full, refer to the split Workers example ↗︎.

Sep 11, 2026

Inspect Voice Agent turn latency and outcomes

Agents

@cloudflare/voice v0.4.0 now lets you inspect where each Voice Agent turn spends time and how it ends.

About the Voice package

The @cloudflare/voice package lets you build real-time voice agents with Cloudflare Agents. It streams microphone audio to an Agent over WebSocket, transcribes speech, runs your model through onTurn(), converts the response to speech, and streams audio back to the caller.

A turn moves through several stages:

Previously, the package's four aggregate metrics covered successful, non-empty speech turns. They did not show how failed, aborted, empty, or text turns ended.

Turn metrics

Each speech or text turn now produces a typed VoiceTurnMetrics summary with:

  • A turnId for correlating events from the same turn.
  • A terminal outcome such as completed, no_output, output_limit, content_filtered, model_error, tts_error, or aborted.
  • Timings for important stages, including speech-to-final-transcript, model-to-first-text, TTS-to-first-audio, and total turn duration.

These timings can overlap and are not additive. Timings for stages that a turn did not reach are omitted.

The latest summary is available through VoiceClient, useVoiceAgent(), and useVoiceInput(). Voice input includes only the speech and transcription timings it can measure.

If an agent produces no audio, you can now distinguish between the model returning no output, reaching an output limit, encountering content filtering, or failing.

Additional diagnostics

For local debugging, you can forward server lifecycle events to the browser console:

The browser console combines server lifecycle events with local microphone, connection, and playback events, including model start, first model text, first audio, and playback start. Diagnostics are off by default, and their event names and fields can change.

VoiceClient also exposes typed events for speech-to-text failures, connection errors, and model outcomes. The SDK removes known content fields and does not read arbitrary provider responses, but custom error messages must not contain sensitive data.

Install the release with a compatible Agents SDK version:

npm i @cloudflare/voice@^0.4.0 agents@^0.22.0
yarn add @cloudflare/voice@^0.4.0 agents@^0.22.0
pnpm add @cloudflare/voice@^0.4.0 agents@^0.22.0
bun add @cloudflare/voice@^0.4.0 agents@^0.22.0

Refer to the Voice pipeline metrics and Voice Agent example ↗︎ to get started.

Aug 3, 2026

Preview: @cloudflare/computer agent runtime

AgentsWorkers

We're releasing an early preview of @cloudflare/computer ↗︎, an open-source agent runtime that gives every agent its own computer. The runtime dynamically orchestrates between fast, efficient isolates and full Linux containers, so the agent always runs on the right compute primitive for the task at hand.

@cloudflare/computer provides a virtual filesystem backed by SQLite, which you can populate from cloud storage, source control, or any files you choose. Agents can read, write, and edit files, run shell commands, and interact with Git repositories. All operations are gated, audited, and observed.

Install the package via npm:

Instantiate a Workspace inside any Durable Object to give your agent a filesystem and execution runtime:

Several execution backends are included or you can write your own:

  • Isolate runtime — fast, horizontally scalable execution via just-bash and Dynamic Workers, ideal for file manipulation and data processing.
  • Container runtime — full Linux environment via Cloudflare Containers, mounted through FUSE, for tasks that need native binaries, package managers, or a complete userland.

The AI SDK-compatible toolkit provides common agent tools (read, write, edit, ls, exec) and guides the model to choose the appropriate backend for each task.

For more examples, including a step-by-step tutorial, visit the @cloudflare/computer repository ↗︎.

Read the announcement blog post for more details: Your agent needs a computer, not a container ↗︎.
